acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Treants family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as World-Tree Warden, T5, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Walking-Forest Sovereign (Sovereign) archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two normal construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: Walking forest with a waterfall down its back, boulders caught in roots, sky-filling canopy, and entire groves on its shoulders.

Signature mechanic: Arena Transformation — Four Seasonal Groves: the waterfall feeds one shoulder grove, boulders lock its root arch, and a lower form performs its learned rule there; resolving it exposes the supply root and drains that grove into a safe path.
battlefieldDuty: Transform a four-grove arena by rerouting a back waterfall through boulder-bound roots and commanding learned lower-form habitats.
constructionDimensions: Family-native, non-affinity tree anatomy, ordinary wood, roots, moss, amber heartwood, the T5 waterfall, and stone in the roots remain botanical, weathered, or carried source motifs—not retired Wood affinity, Earth affinity, or Water affinity.
Sap, lichen, leaves, nests, mushrooms, bark scars, growth rings, and ordinary gravity-driven water remain restrained natural details with no elemental substitution.
counterplay: Answer the called lower-form lesson, then sever the exposed supply root; each drained grove removes one command and opens the sovereign trunk. Affinity signal: The established shallow root, branch load, vine knot, heartwood cavity, or sovereign root-grove anchor remains visible.
forbiddenTreatments: Presenting ordinary wood, moss, waterfall, or stone as an affinity
identityInvariants: Vertical trunk body, root-cluster legs, long branch arms, a bark-suggested face, and canopy remain recognizable.
Bark brown and grey, moss green, autumn gold, sap, and restrained amber heartwood remain botanical materials.
Nests, vines, mushrooms, bark runes, scars, and growth rings record age without replacing readable joints.
Girth, canopy, rooted reach, and resident ecosystems escalate while branch load and root commitment preserve counterplay.
telegraph: Waterfall flow bends toward one shoulder grove, its caught boulders grind, and the matching lower-form marker appears beneath the sky-filling canopy.
